Diego / Marissa,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. Our security team reviewed the TOMs exhibit and surfaced three items we'd like to align on before we sign:

1) BYOK / HSM model — we prefer an HSM-backed BYOK option with customer-managed keys; we need clarity on key custody and emergency access (key escrow/rotation procedures).
2) Key rotation and export controls — please confirm support for 30/90/180-day rotation cadence and how rotation impacts active KV caches (we're concerned about short-term latency spikes).
3) Audit evidence — we need a statement of what logs you can provide (KMS request logs, key material access, key deletion events) and the retention window.

Can you share a proposed update to the TOMs exhibit that captures the BYOK flow and an evidence checklist? We will need Legal to review any new DPA language as well.

Head of Security, Acme Cloud
anna.kim@acme-cloud.com

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: initial DPA + TOMs questions (KMS exhibit)

Anna — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) BYOK / HSM model: Redwood supports two modes: Redwood-managed KMS (default) and BYOK via HSM (customer keys stored in your HSM and extended via PKCS#11 or cloud HSM integration). For BYOK we propose: no Redwood access to raw key material, customer retains root key in their HSM, Redwood receives wrapped keys under customer policy. We can add a short clause to the TOMs exhibit describing the handshake and emergency key rotation (see attached diff).

2) Rotation and KV cache: rotation is supported at arbitrary cadence; recommended best practice is staggered rotation (hot key windows) to avoid cache thrash. We've added a runbook excerpt explaining how we replay/rehydrate KV caches during key rollover — minimal expected latency impact (single-digit ms increase at token level; bucketed during background re-encryption).

3) Audit evidence: we can provide KMS request logs (requester, key-id, operation, timestamp), key lifecycle events (create/import/rotate/deactivate/delete), and HSM audit pointers. Retention: 90 days by default; 1 year available as an add-on. We'll include a sample log schema in the exhibit.

Next steps:
- Marissa: attach the annotated TOMs exhibit (redline) and a short runbook excerpt for rotation.
- Rishi: propose DPA language for BYOK non-access and key custody (legal language) and confirm this covers our support matrix.

We can route final DPA via DocuSign. I will coordinate with Procurement (Acme) on signer order.

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Enterprise Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Anna — attaching the redlined TOMs exhibit and a short rotation runbook excerpt as promised. Highlights in the exhibit:
- Section 2.1: BYOK handshake (PKCS#11/Cloud HSM) with explicit statement that Redwood does not possess unwrapped customer key material.
- Section 2.3: Emergency key recovery — option A (customer escrow with secure transfer) and option B (time-bound emergency unwrap with dual-signer approval; we included an audit trail requirement).
- Section 3.2: Log schema and retention options (90d default, 365d enterprise).

Small ask: can Acme confirm whether they prefer option A or B for emergency access? That choice will drive the exact DPA clause.

I've also drafted the DPA paragraph that Rishi suggested and attached it as a separate doc for legal redline. If Acme is good with Option A (customer escrow), execution can proceed with the following DocuSign flow:
1) Redwood signs (Marissa)

3) Acme procurement/contracting (Michael)

Thanks, Marissa — I reviewed the redline and the BYOK paragraph. Acme prefers Option A (customer escrow) with two caveats:

1) Escrow access must be governed by a documented process and require written request plus confirmation from Acme security contacts; escrowed material must be encrypted at rest with an escrow-specific KMS and limited retention (no longer than 2 years).
2) Redwood must provide a weekly digest of key lifecycle events during the first 90 days post-signing and co-ordinate a post-mortem if any emergency unwrap occurs.

We are OK to proceed with the DocuSign flow once you accept those caveats and confirm the wording in the DPA paragraph. Also cc'ing our procurement mailbox to coordinate the signer order and PO terms.

Michael Hsu
Sr. Counsel, Data & Privacy
Acme Cloud
